subtitle: From Lake Palace Dreams to the Union’s Edge

panels.shot: split composition, left half a glowing Neermahal on Rudrasagar Lake at dusk, right half Kanchan Prava Devi in a dim chamber before a merger document, faint outline of India behind
panels.action: Maharaja Bir Bikram stands in regal youth on Neermahal’s terrace above Rudrasagar Lake while, across the frame, an older, composed Kanchan Prava Devi sits at a desk in New Delhi-era attire, hand hovering over a merger agreement.

dialogue.text: He dreamt Neermahal on Rudrasagar and tribal reserves in the hills; she, his widow, would later sign Tripura itself into the Union. How did a lake palace lead to a nation’s edge?

i18n.hi: उसने रुद्रसागर पर नीर्महल और पहाड़ियों में जनजातीय रिज़र्व सोचे; उसकी बेवा ने आगे चलकर पूरे त्रिपुरा को यूनियन में लिख दिया। एक झील महल से देश की सरहद तक सफ़र कैसे पहुँचा?

panels.shot: slow push-in on young Bir Bikram in coronation regalia in Agartala palace hall
panels.action: A young Maharaja Bir Bikram, in white durbar robes and jewelled turban, stands beneath chandeliers in the Agartala palace, British officers and Tripuri nobles flanking him in a formal coronation scene.

dialogue.text: In 1923, as empires tottered and the Raj watched, Bir Bikram Kishore Manikya took the Tripura throne—last in a long Manikya line, first to rule a world of railways, radios and restless nationalism.

i18n.hi: 1923 में, जब साम्राज्य डगमगा रहे थे और राज देख रहा था, बीर बिक्रम किशोर माणिक्य ने त्रिपुरा की गद्दी संभाली—लंबी माणिक्य वंश की आख़िरी कड़ी, रेल, रेडियो और बेचैन राष्ट्रवाद वाली दुनिया के पहले शासक।

panels.shot: bird’s-eye wide over Agartala town and palace grounds, blending old and new structures
panels.action: From above, the old palace domes and temple spires of Agartala blend with new construction sites, with scaffolding around a large college building and a cleared strip of land that hints at an emerging airfield.

dialogue.text: He inherited a forested, river-cut kingdom between Bengal and the Lushai hills. He would leave behind colleges, runways and reforms that made people call him the architect of modern Tripura.

i18n.hi: उसने घने जंगलों और नदियों से कटी, बंगाल और लुशाई पहाड़ियों के बीच की रियासत पाई। वो पीछे छोड़ गया कॉलेज, रनवे और सुधार, जिनके लिए लोग उसे आधुनिक त्रिपुरा का शिल्पी कहने लगे।

panels.shot: medium-wide of Neermahal construction site on Rudrasagar lake, low angle from water level
panels.action: Labourers pole boats laden with bricks toward scaffolding rising from Rudrasagar Lake while Bir Bikram, in light summer attire, stands on a temporary jetty, gesturing toward the half-built Neermahal with quiet pride.

dialogue.text: On Rudrasagar Lake he raised Neermahal, a water palace finished around 1930—pleasure retreat, symbol of continuity, and a statement that Tripura’s court still had the skill and means to build.

i18n.hi: रुद्रसागर झील पर उसने नीर्महल उठाया, जो 1930 के आस‑पास पूरा हुआ—आनंद महल, परंपरा का निशान, और ये एलान कि त्रिपुरा दरबार में अब भी हुनर और हिम्मत बची है।

panels.shot: interior wide of Neermahal courtyard, light streaming in, mix of royal and common visitors
panels.action: Inside Neermahal’s courtyard, Bir Bikram walks with architects and courtiers, while musicians rehearse in a corner and villagers from nearby areas gaze up at the arches and balconies in quiet awe.

dialogue.text: Neermahal was not only a royal escape. Its corridors carried musicians’ ragas, ministers’ debates and the Maharaja’s sense that Tripura must open to the modern world without abandoning its own style.

i18n.hi: नीर्महल सिर्फ़ शाही सैरगाह नहीं था। उसकी गलियों में कलाकारों की राग, मंत्रियों की बहसें और महाराजा का ये यक़ीन गूँजता था कि त्रिपुरा को दुनिया से जुड़ना है, पर अपने ढंग से।

panels.shot: classroom interior, mid shot of Maharaja visiting students at Maharaja Bir Bikram College
panels.action: In a new college classroom, young men in dhotis and shirts sit at wooden desks as Bir Bikram, in a simple achkan, leans over a map on a student’s table while a British-educated professor watches.

dialogue.text: He founded institutions like Maharaja Bir Bikram College, sensing that future Tripuris would need more than swords and titles. Knowledge, he believed, was the new shield of a small state.

i18n.hi: उसने महाराजा बीर बिक्रम कॉलेज जैसे संस्थान खोले, समझते हुए कि आने वाली पीढ़ियों को तलवार और ख़िताब से ज़्यादा चाहिए। उसके लिए ज्ञान ही छोटे राज्य की नई ढाल था।

panels.shot: low-angle wide of an early airstrip with a small plane, Bir Bikram inspecting
panels.action: On a rough airstrip outside Agartala, a small propeller aircraft rests as Bir Bikram, flanked by officers, inspects the runway, the wind tugging at his coat while workers clear stones in the background.

dialogue.text: He pushed for an airfield at Agartala, bringing Tripura into the network of runways that spanned the subcontinent. The kingdom’s isolation began to crack as planes traced new paths over the bamboo groves.

i18n.hi: उसने अगरतला में हवाई पट्टी पर ज़ोर लगाया, त्रिपुरा को उन रनवे से जोड़ा जो पूरे उपमहाद्वीप में फैले थे। बाँस के जंगलों के ऊपर जब जहाज़ नई रेखाएँ खींचने लगे, तो रियासत की तन्हाई में पहली दरार पड़ी।

panels.shot: wide shot in hilly interior, Maharaja with tribal elders amid forest clearings
panels.action: In a forested hill village, Bir Bikram sits on a wooden bench beneath tall trees with Indigenous Tiprasa elders in traditional attire, spread-out maps showing shaded reserve areas between them.

dialogue.text: Beyond palaces and planes, he marked land for Indigenous Tiprasa communities—reserves within his state. Later scholars would see in these maps the early lineaments of Tripura’s tribal autonomous areas.

i18n.hi: महलों और जहाज़ों से आगे बढ़कर, उसने अपने राज्य में मूल निवासी टिप्रासा समाज के लिए ज़मीन चिन्हित की—आरक्षित क्षेत्र। बाद के विद्वानों ने इन्हीं नक्शों में त्रिपुरा के जनजातीय स्वायत्त इलाकों की शुरुआती रेखाएँ देखीं।

panels.shot: medium close-up on Bir Bikram and a Tiprasa elder clasping hands, forest behind
panels.action: Bir Bikram clasps the weathered hands of a Tiprasa elder, their faces serious, the dense green of the hills behind them hinting at the lands being discussed.

dialogue.speaker: bir_bikram_and_kanchan_prava_devi
dialogue.text: These hills are your home. The law must remember that.

i18n.hi: ये पहाड़ तुम्हारा घर हैं। क़ानून को ये याद रखना होगा।

panels.shot: dim interior of palace study at night, map of India and world on the wall
panels.action: At night in his study, Bir Bikram sits at a large desk lit by a single lamp, a globe and maps showing British India and the wider world spread before him, letters from abroad stacked neatly.

dialogue.text: He travelled beyond Tripura and watched other lands change. In his study, under the quiet whir of a fan, he traced news of world wars, nationalist stirrings and the slow re-drawing of maps.

i18n.hi: वो त्रिपुरा से बाहर भी गया और बदलती दुनिया को देखा। अपने अध्ययन कक्ष में, पंखे की धीमी आवाज़ के नीचे, वो विश्वयुद्धों की ख़बरें, राष्ट्रवादी लहरें और नक्शों के धीरे‑धीरे बदलते रंग टटोलता रहा।

panels.shot: transition shot, calendar pages flipping from early 1940s to 1947, overlaid on palace corridor
panels.action: A corridor of the palace fades behind the image of calendar pages tearing away, dates racing toward 1947 as servants move hurriedly and courtiers whisper in anxious clusters.

dialogue.text: The 1940s brought war across Asia and hunger closer home. By 1947 the British prepared to leave. For princely states like Tripura, questions that had been distant suddenly stood at the door.

i18n.hi: 1940 का दशक एशिया पर जंग और घर के क़रीब भुखमरी लेकर आया। 1947 तक अंग्रेज़ जाने की तैयारी कर रहे थे। त्रिपुरा जैसी रियासतों के लिए, जो सवाल दूर लगते थे, अचानक दरवाज़े पर खड़े हो गए।

panels.shot: intimate interior shot of Bir Bikram and Kanchan Prava Devi sitting together in a quiet palace room
panels.action: Bir Bikram and Kanchan Prava Devi sit side by side on a low divan, a window behind them opening to Neermahal’s silhouette in the distance, their faces thoughtful as if sharing unspoken concerns.

dialogue.speaker: bir_bikram_and_kanchan_prava_devi
dialogue.text: The world is shifting, Kanchan. Our son must walk a different path.

i18n.hi: दुनिया बदल रही है, कंचन। हमारे बेटे को अलग राह पर चलना होगा।

panels.shot: somber palace chamber, low light, focus on Kanchan Prava Devi in widow’s white
panels.action: In a quiet chamber draped in white, Kanchan Prava Devi, now in simple widow’s attire, sits poised yet grief-stricken beside a low bier where Bir Bikram’s portrait and garlands rest, courtiers standing at a respectful distance.

dialogue.text: In 1947, before the new India fully emerged, Bir Bikram died. His son, Kirit Bikram, was still a child. His widow, Kanchan Prava Devi, stepped from consort to regent in a kingdom entering its hardest years.

i18n.hi: 1947 में, जब नया भारत पूरी तरह बना भी नहीं था, बीर बिक्रम चल बसे। उनका बेटा, किरीट बिक्रम, अभी बच्चा था। उनकी बेगम, कंचन प्रभा देवी, सहधर्मिणी से रीजेंट बनकर उस रियासत की कमान में आई जो अपने सबसे कठिन दौर में दाख़िल हो रही थी।

panels.shot: low-angle shot of Kanchan Prava Devi on a throne-like chair in durbar hall, child prince beside her
panels.action: In the durbar hall, Kanchan Prava Devi sits upright on the state chair with the young Kirit Bikram beside her, officials bowing as they present files while portraits of past Manikya rulers loom from the walls.

dialogue.text: She held the regency in her son’s name, balancing court factions, British withdrawal and the birth of two new Dominions. Her duty was no longer only to a dynasty, but to a people caught between frontiers.

i18n.hi: उसने बेटे के नाम पर रीजेंसी संभाली, दरबार की खेमा‑बाज़ी, अंग्रेज़ी रवानगी और दो नए डोमिनियन के जन्म के बीच संतुलन रखा। अब उसका फ़र्ज़ सिर्फ़ वंश नहीं, उन लोगों से भी था जो दो सरहदों के बीच फँस गए थे।

panels.shot: map-table top-down shot, showing Tripura flanked by India and East Pakistan, hands pointing
panels.action: On a table, a detailed map shows Tripura nestled between the new India and East Pakistan; Kanchan Prava Devi’s hand rests on Tripura while an Indian official’s hand indicates the borders and arrows of refugee movement.

dialogue.text: Partition split Bengal and created East Pakistan to Tripura’s west and south. Refugees poured across rivers and roads. The small hill kingdom found itself facing demographic pressure and security fears at once.

i18n.hi: बँटवारे ने बंगाल को चीर दिया और त्रिपुरा के पश्चिम और दक्षिण में पूर्वी पाकिस्तान बना। शरणार्थी नदियों और सड़कों के ज़रिए टूट पड़े। छोटी पहाड़ी रियासत पर एक साथ आबादी का दबाव और सुरक्षा की दहशत आ गिरी।

panels.shot: busy border road shot, refugees walking with bundles, Tripura soldiers watching
panels.action: Lines of refugees carrying bundles and leading children walk along a dusty road into Tripura, while a few Tripura soldiers and officials watch solemnly, the distant outline of a border gate barely visible.

dialogue.text: Each group that arrived brought stories of loss and fear. In the hills, Tiprasa communities worried about their lands. In Agartala, the regent weighed how long Tripura could stand alone between new nations.

i18n.hi: हर नया जत्था अपने साथ डर और बिखराव की दास्तानें लाया। पहाड़ियों में टिप्रासा समाज अपनी ज़मीनों को लेकर घबराया। अगरतला में रीजेंट सोचती रही कि दो नए मुल्कों के बीच त्रिपुरा कब तक अकेला खड़ा रह सकता है।

panels.shot: New Delhi office interior, medium shot of Kanchan Prava Devi across a desk from Indian leaders
panels.action: In a plain New Delhi government office, Kanchan Prava Devi, dignified in a white sari, sits at a desk opposite Indian officials in Western suits and khadi, papers between them, the atmosphere heavy but formal.

dialogue.text: New Delhi pressed for integration. Letters from leaders like Sardar Patel made clear the Union’s resolve. The choice was framed not as whether Tripura would merge, but on what terms and when.

i18n.hi: नई दिल्ली लगातार जोड़ने पर अड़ी रही। सरदार पटेल जैसे नेताओं के ख़तों ने यूनियन की सख़्त मंशा साफ़ कर दी। सवाल ये नहीं बचा कि त्रिपुरा जुड़ेगा या नहीं, बल्कि ये कि कब और किस शर्त पर।

panels.shot: close-up on Kanchan Prava Devi’s face, contemplative, overlaid faintly with images of hills and palace
panels.action: A tight close-up of Kanchan Prava Devi’s steady yet troubled gaze, faint reflections of Tripura’s hills and the Agartala palace suggested in the shadows around her.

dialogue.speaker: bir_bikram_and_kanchan_prava_devi
dialogue.text: If the crown must bend, let the people not break.

i18n.hi: अगर ताज झुके, तो लोग न टूटें।

panels.shot: table close-up on the Tripura Merger Agreement, pen poised in Kanchan’s hand
panels.action: The Tripura Merger Agreement lies open on a polished desk, the words clearly laid out though unreadable in the image, as Kanchan Prava Devi’s hand holds a pen just above the signature line.

dialogue.text: On 9 September 1949 she signed the Tripura Merger Agreement. A pressured, strategic choice, it ended formal Manikya sovereignty, but set conditions for administration and safeguards as Tripura entered the Indian Union.

i18n.hi: 9 सितंबर 1949 को उसने त्रिपुरा मर्जर एग्रीमेंट पर दस्तख़त किए। दबाव और रणनीति में लिया गया फ़ैसला, जिसने माणिक्य राज की औपचारिक हकूमत ख़त्म कर दी, पर साथ ही प्रशासन और सुरक्षा की कुछ शर्तें भी बाँधीं, जब त्रिपुरा भारतीय यूनियन में घुला।

panels.shot: ceremonial wide shot of flag change in Agartala, old royal flag lowered, Indian flag raised
panels.action: In a public square at Agartala, Tripura’s royal flag is being gently lowered from a high mast while, on another mast, the Indian tricolour rises, officials and townspeople watching in respectful silence.

dialogue.text: On 15 October 1949 the merger took effect. The royal standard came down, the tricolour rose. For some it was relief, for others quiet mourning—but for all, a line had been crossed that would not be walked back.

i18n.hi: 15 अक्टूबर 1949 को विलय लागू हुआ। शाही निशान नीचे उतरा, तिरंगा ऊपर चढ़ा। कुछ के लिए ये राहत थी, कुछ के लिए धीमा मातम—पर सबके लिए, एक ऐसी रेखा पार हो चुकी थी जो वापस नहीं मुड़नी थी।

panels.shot: wide shot of modern Tripura hills with a Tribal Areas signpost, Neermahal distant on the lake
panels.action: In a present-day style scene, lush Tripura hills carry a modest signpost marking a tribal autonomous area, while far off Rudrasagar Lake shimmers with Neermahal still standing, its white form small but distinct.

dialogue.text: Later, Tripura’s tribal autonomous council would echo Bir Bikram’s reserves, and Neermahal would still float on Rudrasagar. A prince and a regent, working in different storms, had tried to guard a future they would never rule.

i18n.hi: बाद में, त्रिपुरा की जनजातीय स्वायत्त परिषद ने बीर बिक्रम के रिज़र्व की गूँज दोहराई, और नीर्महल अब भी रुद्रसागर पर तैरता रहा। एक राजकुमार और एक रीजेंट, अलग‑अलग तूफ़ानों में, एक ऐसे भविष्य की रखवाली करते रहे जिसे वो ख़ुद कभी शासन नहीं कर पाए।

title_i18n.en: Bir Bikram's Reserve and the Merger
title_i18n.hi: बीर बिक्रम का आरक्षित इलाका और विलय

subtitle_i18n.en: From Lake Palace Dreams to the Union’s Edge
subtitle_i18n.hi: झील महल के ख़्वाब से यूनियन की सरहद तक
